Griffin: $20 Million Series B Funding Led By Octagon Partners To Expand Card Issuing And Stablecoin Banking Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:49 AM
Griffin: $20 Million Series B Funding Led By Octagon Partners To Expand Card Issuing And Stablecoin Banking Services
Griffin, a United Kingdom-based licensed bank providing embedded banking infrastructure to fintech companies and technology platforms, has raised $20 million in Series B funding led by Octagon Partners. Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja, Breega, and other existing investors participated in the round, which values Griffin at more than $100 million.
The financing will support the expansion of Griffin’s banking platform into card issuing and stablecoin-related services while providing capital for continued growth toward profitability.
Griffin operates a regulated banking infrastructure platform that enables businesses to integrate accounts, payments, and compliance capabilities into their products.
The company serves more than 80 businesses, including Uber, Countingup, Anna Money, Yonder, and Prosper.
Its infrastructure supports more than 300,000 underlying retail and business customers and processes nearly 10 million payments annually.
The latest investment comes approximately two years after Griffin began operating as a fully licensed UK bank.
Expanding Into Debit And Credit Card Issuing
Griffin plans to use the Series B financing to introduce card issuing capabilities.
The initial offering will enable customers to launch branded retail and corporate debit cards using Griffin’s banking infrastructure.
This will extend the company’s existing services beyond accounts and payments.
Businesses using Griffin’s platform will be able to combine banking accounts, payment processing, and card products through a single infrastructure provider.
The company also intends to introduce credit card capabilities following the initial debit card launch.
These services are designed for fintech businesses and other technology companies that want to offer financial products without independently developing every component of the underlying banking infrastructure.
Griffin believes adding cards will strengthen its relationships with existing customers while creating opportunities to serve additional businesses.
The expanded platform will provide more options for companies developing financial services embedded within their own applications.
Developing Stablecoin Payment Infrastructure
The second major area of investment involves stablecoin-related banking services.
Griffin plans to develop reserve capabilities for businesses operating in the stablecoin market.
The company also intends to integrate on-chain cross-border payments into its platform.
Stablecoins are digital assets designed to maintain a relatively stable value, often by referencing a conventional currency.
Businesses developing stablecoin-based financial services may require banking relationships, reserve management arrangements, and payment infrastructure.
Griffin’s planned capabilities are intended to support these requirements.
The company’s existing regulated banking operations provide a foundation for developing additional services.
The stablecoin initiatives remain planned product developments rather than capabilities that the announcement identifies as fully launched.

Accountable Launches to Give Power to American Taxpayers
News provided by
Accountable
Nov 16, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Co-founded by Acorns CEO Noah Kerner and Jeff Cruttenden, Accountable raises $20 million to help Americans file their taxes, follow their money, and ultimately decide how it is spent.
NEW YORK , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Accountable, a new consumer tax and civic company, launched its waitlist today with the belief that taxpayers should be treated like investors in the country they fund. Investors expect transparency into how their money is put to work, accountability for how it is managed, and a voice in the decisions that shape where it goes. Taxpayers deserve the same.
Continue Reading
Every year, Americans file more than 160 million federal income tax returns, while individuals— not corporations—account for roughly 85% of federal tax revenue. The average taxpayer spends about 12 hours preparing and completing a return, only to be left with a larger question once it's filed: what did their money actually pay for?
Co-founded by Acorns CEO Noah Kerner and Jeff Cruttenden, Accountable Launches to Give Power to American Taxpayers.
Post this
Accountable's first product, a tax filing platform designed around the needs of the taxpayer, will launch in January 2027 ahead of tax season. With a filer's permission, Accountable retrieves available tax information and documents, prefills their return, and guides them through reviewing and submitting for one flat price of $76, with filing free for anyone experiencing financial hardship. Accountable customers will also receive a personalized taxpayer receipt showing an estimated breakdown of what their taxes fund across federal, state, and local government spending.
"Cumulatively, taxes are the largest check most of us will ever write, and it's ridiculous that we don't even get a receipt," said Noah Kerner, co-founder of Accountable. "Taxpayers deserve a better experience: smart, fast and fair filing, transparency into what we're paying for, and power over where our money goes. After all, it's our money, we fund this country, and we should feel like shareholders in it."
The filing platform is the first step in Accountable's broader vision: help Americans file their taxes, follow their money and, over time, have a greater voice in how it is spent. Accountable is starting with filing because it is the most direct financial interaction most Americans have with government. Each year, Americans are asked to account for every dollar they earn. Accountability should go both ways.
For Kerner, Accountable is a continuation of a career spent giving everyday people more access and agency in complex financial systems. At Acorns, Kerner has helped over 15 million everyday Americans save & invest over $30 billion. At Say, he gave individual investors a voice in the companies they own. At Accountable, he wants to give taxpayers the same voice in the country they fund. The full team behind Accountable comes with a wealth of experience across tax, civic, investing, health, and consumer technology sectors.
"We backed Accountable because we believe the taxpayer is one of the biggest consumer categories still waiting to be reinvented," said Lauren Kolodny, Founding Partner at Acrew Capital . articles.text:
Fresh Off $20M Series A, WhiteMatter Taps Leaders from Proofpoint and Hitachi to Scale Globally
News provided by
WhiteMatter
Nov 17, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Jasmine Wu joins as Chief Marketing Officer and Anuj Gupta as Managing Director, Asia Pacific & Japan
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following its $20 million Series A at a $202 million valuation and fivefold revenue growth in six months, WhiteMatter , formerly QuilrAI, today announced two senior hires to accelerate its global expansion. Jasmine Wu, formerly senior marketing executive of Proofpoint and ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, joins WhiteMatter as Chief Marketing Officer, while Anuj Gupta, former Managing Director of Hitachi Systems India, joins as Managing Director, Asia Pacific & Japan (APJ). They join Chief Revenue Officer Tammy Sexton, who joined in late 2025, as WhiteMatter builds out its leadership team to meet growing global demand for AI agent governance.
Continue Reading
Jasmine Wu joins as Chief Marketing Officer and Anuj Gupta as Managing Director, Asia Pacific & Japan
WhiteMatter was founded by CEO Vidit Arora, a founding member of Securonix who spent more than a decade helping build the security analytics company, leading across product, solution architecture, and global customer experience. He created WhiteMatter to solve a new security challenge: how companies govern AI agents that can make decisions, access systems, and take action on their own. WhiteMatter helps enterprises assess and approve agents before they go live, then continuously control what they can access and do in production. The company has received acquisition offers but is instead focusing on building and scaling the business independently. The new appointments bring the marketing, sales, and leadership needed to support that growth.
"When AI began moving from a tool people use to agents that make autonomous decisions, I watched the traditional security model start to break," said Arora. "I founded WhiteMatter on the belief that companies would need to rethink security and infrastructure for a world built around AI and agents. That world is here. Enterprises are scaling agents now, and they need governance based on how agents actually behave, starting from pre-production blueprints. Jasmine, Anuj, and Tammy have each built and scaled category-defining businesses, and they give us the go-to-market strength to deliver that governance worldwide."
Wu joins from Proofpoint, where she served as Head of Product Marketing and GTM Operations as the company grew from under $1 billion to more than $2 billion in annual recurring revenue. Before that, she was Head of Marketing at ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok. Her career spans 15+ years across security and consumer technology at global scale. At WhiteMatter, she will lead global marketing to establish WhiteMatter as the company defining the agent and AI lifecycle governance category.
"The AI and agent challenge extends far beyond security, yet it has been treated as a security problem for too long," said Wu. "Enterprises are deploying thousands of agents and AI workflows powered by non-deterministic models, but runtime protection alone cannot govern an agent that was never properly assessed before deployment.
